samples.report:
I have enough to build the full analysis. Let me note the key reconciliation I worked through before writing: the filed FCF does **not** deduct SBC, and the Section 6 "change in WC" is incomplete for a marketplace (it omits deferred revenue), so I anchor FCF to the filed OCF/FCF and deduct SBC explicitly rather than bridging from operating income. I also corrected my net-debt figure — EXPE is modestly **net debt** (~$0.7B), not net cash, which materially lowers intrinsic value vs. a naive read.

Below is the complete report.

```
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  EXPEDIA GROUP, INC. (EXPE) — RS2 v2.0 INTEGRATED ANALYSIS
  T0 = 2026-08-23/24 | Price $321.63 | Mkt Cap $38.594B
════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

SECTION 0. ANALYSIS OVERVIEW
────────────────────────────
Enterprise: Asset-light online travel marketplace (B2C brands Expedia/
Hotels.com/Vrbo + largest B2B travel business + advertising/trivago).
Fiscal year ends 12-31. T-1 = FY2025 (filed 2026-02-12). TTM = through
2026-06-30 (filed 2026-08-06).

Core tension of this analysis: EXPE is a high-ROIC (~46% [Estimate]),
asset-light FCF machine trading at a LOW multiple (7.5x EV/TTM-FCF
[Estimate]; 13.7x 2027E P/E [Estimate]) — a large discount to peer
Booking (~25x) and Airbnb (~40x). The discount reflects perceived
cyclicality, US concentration, competitive threat (Airbnb/Booking/
Google), a "narrow moat" label, dual-class control (Diller ~32% voting
[Actual via 10-K]), and recent short-seller/activist attention.
The stock has ALSO already run up ~25% since Apr-2026 and sits within
4% of its 52-wk high ($333.24). So the question is not "is the business
good?" (yes) but "is the multiple justified, and is THIS price a good
entry after the run?"

My verdict: Business quality is High; the stock is FAIRLY valued to
MODERATELY undervalued at $321.63 (base-case IV ~$380, MoS ~15%). The
most conservative DCF corner (~$323) is essentially AT the current
price. This is a HOLD/ACCUMULATE-on-weakness, not a deep-value BUY.
Conviction: High (11/15). Sizing: 4-5%, scale-in.

Data reliability note: I did NOT rely on any suspicious series step
(no Philip-Morris-style basis change detected in the revenue series).
Key gaps handled: marketable securities & lease liabilities NOT in pack
(net debt imprecise); SBC per-year NOT in pack (used FY2025 $398M
[Actual via IR] + Q1-2026 $103M run-rate [Estimate]); effective tax
rate withheld from pack (used 20.0% [Actual via FY2025 IR release]);
capitalized software capex NOT in pack (filed capex = PP&E only, so
filed FCF is likely slightly OVERSTATED — carried as a downside).

SECTION 1. MACRO CONTEXT
────────────────────────
[Retrieved, Aug 2026, secondary]:
- 10Y Treasury: ~4.7% (4.69-4.73%), +45bps y/y, above 4.25% long-avg.
  Direction: roughly flat-to-up over the past month. [Estimate]
- CPI: 3.4% y/y (Jul-2026), down from 3.5% (Jun); energy +14.7% —
  STICKY, not disinflating. [Actual via BLS]
- DXY: ~98.8, lowest since ~May-29-2026 — WEAK dollar. [Estimate]
- Fed: cut at Sep-2025 meeting; mortgage rates trended down through
  Q4-2025. Current exact target range NOT confirmed in my searches
  [Unconfirmed]. Stance: easing cycle begun but constrained by sticky
  inflation → "higher-for-longer with cuts" (neutral-to-easing).

Regime probability distribution (must sum to 100%):
- Goldilocks (low-ish rates + growth): 30%
- Reflation (higher rates + growth): 35%  ← sticky 3.4% CPI + 4.7% 10Y
- Stagflation (higher rates + low growth): 20%
- Recession (low rates + low growth): 15%

Enterprise/sector macro sensitivity (each -3..+3):
- Interest-rate sensitivity: -1 (travel is discretionary; higher rates
  mildly suppress big-ticket travel; offset by weak-dollar tailwind)
- Dollar sensitivity: +2 (WEAK dollar = tailwind: (a) non-US revenue
  ~40% of total and the FASTER-growing segment [Actual: non-US +18%
  vs US +12% in Q2-26] translates to more USD; (b) cheaper US outbound
  travel = demand tailwind)
- Liquidity sensitivity: +1
- Economic-cycle sensitivity: -2 (travel is pro-cyclical/discretionary;
  a US recession is the key bear trigger)
- Commodity sensitivity: -1 (fuel/energy costs; energy +14.7% CPI is a
  mild cost + demand headwind)

Macro alignment: The weak dollar is a genuine TAILWIND (+2 on the
largest sensitivity axis), partially offset by sticky inflation / a
pro-cyclical business in a Reflation-leaning regime. Net: MILD
TAILWIND → Conviction +0.5 step (capped; does not change IV, only
entry timing/size). I treat macro as mildly supportive but NOT the
driver — the driver is company-specific FCF + multiple.

SECTION 1.5. BASE RATE CHECK
────────────────────────────
- Base rate: a "narrow-moat" consumer-discretionary platform sustaining
  >15% EPS CAGR for 5+ years: ~25-35% [Assumption, base-rate prior].
- EXPE has delivered 20 consecutive quarters of double-digit B2B growth
  [Actual via IR] and 3+ years of Adj-EBITDA margin expansion
  [Actual: 23.8% FY25, +368bps in Q4-25]. This is ABOVE base rate.
- Deviation justification (need 3+):
  (1) Asset-light structure → 46% ROIC [Estimate], far above the
      typical consumer platform;
  (2) B2B mix shift (35% of rev, +21-24%, higher 13.9% take rate vs
      B2C 11.5% [Actual via segment P&L]) is a structural, not
      cyclical, margin driver;
  (3) Scale + first-party data + OneKey loyalty create real (if
      narrow) switching costs.
- Base-rate shock check: My base-case assumes continued (decelerating)
  out-performance. Success prob is ~1.3-1.5x base rate → NOT a red
  flag, but I do NOT assume the out-performance accelerates. I model
  DECELERATION (9.4% → ~4% by 2030). This keeps me inside the base
  rate envelope.

SECTION 2. BUSINESS QUALITY
────────────────────────────
What it does (3 sentences): EXPE is a global travel marketplace that
earns a take-rate (revenue/gross-bookings ~12-13%) on lodging, air,
car, cruise and vacation-rental bookings across its consumer brands
(Expedia, Hotels.com, Vrbo), its B2B white-label/travel-agent platform,
and an advertising network (incl. trivago). It is asset-light: it does
not own inventory, so gross bookings (~$120B) are ~8x revenue
(~$14.7B). It monetizes scale via supply partnerships, first-party
traveler data, and the OneKey loyalty program.
Understandability: HIGH.

Moat (0-3 each):
- Intangible (brand/trademarks, 3 flagship brands): 2
- Switching costs (OneKey loyalty, B2B integration, corporate travel
  workflows): 2
- Network effects (two-sided: travelers ↔ hotels/supply; ad network): 2
- Cost advantage (scale in supply deals, tech/AI leverage): 2
- Economies of scale: 2
- Regulatory barriers: 1
- Data moat (first-party booking data, personalization): 2
TOTAL = 13 → WIDE moat (11-15). Direction: STABLE-to-WIDENING on B2B
+ data; STABLE on B2C. (Note: third parties rate it "narrow"; I score
it wide-on-paper but apply a market discount for durability — see Red
Team. The honest read is "narrow-to-wide, with real competitive
erosion risk.")

Lynch: FAST GROWER / STALWART hybrid. Checkpoints: growth is real but
decelerating (fast-grower fading into stalwart); margins expanding;
FCF strong; the risk is the growth rate normalizing to high-single/
low-double digits.

Financial strength scorecard [Actual unless noted]:
- Revenue growth: 5-yr CAGR +23.2% (pack, inflated by post-COVID
  recovery); FY25 +8%; TTM +~7%; Q2-26 +14% (re-accelerating).
- Operating margin: FY25 12.7%; 12-yr median 6.9%; TTM ~13-14%.
  Expanding.
- ROE: 89.5% (pack, vendor — extremely high, reflects thin equity base
  from buybacks). ROIC ~46% [Estimate] (NOPAT $1,497M / IC ~$3,262M).
  Both far above WACC → value-creating.
- FCF margin: FY25 21.1% (filed FCF $3,110M); SBC-adjusted 18.4%
  [Estimate]. TTM 28.4% (elevated, timing).
- Net debt: ~$0.7B [Estimate] (total debt $6.415B [vendor] − cash+ST
  inv $5.7B [filed FY25]). Interest coverage very high.
Judgment: EXCELLENT (asset-light, high ROIC, strong FCF, minimal net
debt). The thin equity base (high ROE) is a buyback artifact, not a
fragility — net debt is low.

Capital allocation (0-3 each, /15):
1. Buyback efficiency: 3 (buying at 13-17x, below historical avg;
   $1.7B/9M sh FY25; new $5B auth; ~$900M in H1-26).
2. M&A track record: 2 (trivago, Vrbo, HomeAway accretive to scale;
   no major impairments; but integration risk on smaller deals).
3. Capex efficiency: 3 (asset-light, capex ~5% of rev, incremental
   ROIC very high).
4. Rationality of mix: 3 (reinvest in B2B/AI + return via buyback +
   20% dividend raise — well balanced).
5. Guidance accuracy: 3 (exceeded high end of Q2-26 guidance; raised
   FY26; consistent beats).
Insider: Diller >5% (Class B, ~32% voting) +1; but dual-class =
governance overhang, and recent insider activity not clearly net-buy
→ net +0 (the control concentration is a double-edged sword).
TOTAL ≈ 14/15 → EXCELLENT capital allocator.

SECTION 2.5. INTANGIBLES-ADJUSTED FINANCIALS
────────────────────────────
- SBC treatment: FY2025 SBC $398M (2.70% of rev) [Actual via
  analystlens/IR]; Q1-2026 $103M (run-rate ~$412M, ~2.6% of rev)
  [Estimate]. I DEDUCT SBC from FCF (real economic cost):
  SBC-adj FCF FY25 = $3,110M − $398M = $2,712M (18.4% margin).
- R&D capitalization: EXPE's "technology & content" spend is largely
  expensed; capitalizing it would RAISE reported ROIC further. I do
  NOT capitalize (conservative) — my 46% ROIC is already high on a
  GAAP-ish basis.
- Operating leases: NOT in pack [Unconfirmed]. Travel marketplaces
  carry some lease liabilities (offices). Likely modest vs. $24.5B
  assets; I note it could add ~$0.3-0.8B to debt [Assumption] —
  immaterial to the conclusion but flagged.
- Brand/data: OneKey + first-party data are real but hard to value;
  I capture their value implicitly in the FCF/multiple, NOT as a
  separate add (avoids double-count).
- Owner earnings (Buffett): ≈ SBC-adj FCF ≈ $2,712M FY25 (18.4% of
  rev). This is the number I grow in the DCF.

SECTION 3. VALUATION — ENGINE 1 (DCF + Multiples), with Engine-3
platform-premium overlay in the Bull case
────────────────────────────
Engine choice: Archetype B (Quality Compounder) → Engine 1. I add an
Engine-3-style platform premium ONLY in the Bull case (B2B + advertising
+ OneKey as a distinct, faster, higher-margin growth engine) — I do NOT
mix it into the base case (Rule 6).

Why not Engine 4 (option-led)? Core is large, profitable, cash-generative
today — value is NOT dominated by future optionality. Why not Engine 2
(cyclical)? ROIC > WACC across the cycle (46%), margins are expanding
not mean-reverting to a low norm; travel cyclicality is real but the
business has compounding features. Engine 1 is correct.

DISCOUNT-RATE DERIVATION (explicit):
- Risk-free (10Y): 4.7% [Retrieved, Aug-2026]
- Equity risk premium: 4.5% [Assumption, developed-mkt mid]
- Beta: 1.246 [Pack, aggregator; window/benchmark unstated]
- Cost of equity = 4.7% + 1.246×4.5% = 10.31%
- Cost of debt (pre): 5.0% [Assumption]; after-tax = 5.0%×(1−0.20)=4.0%
- Weights: Equity $38.594B / (Equity + net debt $0.715B) → E 98.2%,
  D 1.8%
- WACC = 0.982×10.31% + 0.018×4.0% = 10.18% → I USE 10.5% for the BASE
  (slightly conservative, and to embed a small cyclicality/competition
  risk premium the 1.246 beta likely understates). Sensitivity at
  9.5% / 11.5%.

EXPLICIT FORECAST (per-year). Revenue path SOURCED; FCF-adj margin is
the key [Assumption] (flagged). Capex & D&A are embedded in the FCF-adj
margin (anchored to filed OCF/FCF, which already net them out correctly
including deferred-revenue WC swings that Section 6 omits).

Driver sourcing:
- Revenue FY26 $16.135B: [Actual] raised guidance midpoint
  ($16.05-16.22B, +9-10%).
- Revenue FY27-30: [Assumption] — decelerating 7.2%→3.9%, anchored to
  (a) consensus 2027 rev growth 7.07% [Pack/Estimate], (b) global
  travel ~4%/yr (Phocuswright $1.6T→$1.8T 2024-27 [Estimate]), (c)
  EXPE's historical share-gain + B2B momentum. NOT a guided figure —
  this is the largest uncertainty. I show the range in scenarios.
- FCF-adj margin: [Assumption] 19.5%→21.0%, driven by guided Adj-EBITDA
  +1.5-1.75pts FY26 [Actual] flowing through + B2B mix + AI, offset by
  SBC growth and (unconfirmed) capitalized-software capex.
- Terminal g: 2.5% [Assumption, ≤ long-run nominal GDP, near travel].

$M table (Base case):
Year   Rev      RevG   FCFadjMgn  FCFadj   (discount @10.5%)
2026   16,135   +9.4%  19.5%      3,146    PV 2,847
2027   17,300   +7.2%  20.0%      3,460    PV 2,834
2028   18,350   +6.1%  20.5%      3,762    PV 2,788
2029   19,250   +4.9%  20.8%      4,004    PV 2,686
2030   20,000   +3.9%  21.0%      4,200    PV 2,549
                                           Σ PV explicit = 13,704

Terminal value (end-2030):
TV = 4,200 × 1.025 / (0.105 − 0.025) = 4,305 / 0.080 = 53,813
PV(TV) = 53,813 / 1.105^5 = 53,813 / 1.6475 = 32,664

EV = 13,704 + 32,664 = 46,368
Less net debt = 715  →  Equity = 45,653
Per share (119.996M) = $380

TORNADO (per-share IV; top-3 sensitive vars become Thesis KPIs):
- Terminal g (2.0%→3.0%): ~$323 → ~$464  (MOST sensitive)
- WACC (11.5%→9.5%):      ~$323 → ~$464  (MOST sensitive)
- FCF-adj margin 2030 (±1pt): ~∓$25/share
- Revenue 2027-30 path (±1pt/yr): ~∓$20/share
→ Top-3 KPIs: (1) long-run FCF margin, (2) long-run growth, (3) the
multiple the market assigns (proxy for perceived risk). The terminal
value is ~70% of EV — this is the dominant uncertainty and I carry it
in scenarios, NOT a point estimate.

Multiples cross-check:
- 2027E EPS $23.41 [Estimate, consensus; wide range 16.86-32.46].
- Base DCF $380 ≈ 16.2x 2027E EPS ≈ 11x 2027E FCF-adj/share (~$34).
- Current $321.63 = 13.7x 2027E EPS = 7.5x TTM EV/FCF.
- So base IV implies a MODERATE re-rating (13.7x→16.2x 2027E P/E), NOT
  a peer-convergence re-rating (which would be 22-25x → the Bull case).
- DCF and multiples CONVERGE at ~$380 (good internal consistency).

SECTION 3.5. SECOND-ORDER EFFECTS
────────────────────────────
Competitive response: If EXPE's B2B + AI succeed, Booking and Airbnb
will (a) accelerate their own B2B/agent tools and (b) bid up hotel
supply costs / marketing. Net impact on EXPE margin: -1 (competitive
response is the main reason I cap FCF-adj margin at 21%, not 24%).
Reflexivity: High stock price → easier M&A currency + talent retention
(positive); but the dual-class + short-seller attention creates a
negative feedback loop if guidance slips (the May-2026 guidance
reiteration caused a dip [brief/Estimate]). Customer behavior: B2C is
mainstream (saturating, +8%); B2B is early-mainstream (+21-24%) — the
mix shift is the second-order growth engine.

SECTION 4. SCENARIOS (Bayesian)
────────────────────────────
Prior (Layer 1.5): out-performance ~1.3-1.5x base rate. Update triggers
observed: Q2-26 beat + raised guidance (positive), short-seller/activist
attention (negative), sticky inflation (mild negative). Posterior
weights below.

BEAR (25%) — IV ~$270:
- US consumer/rate shock → travel demand softens; rev growth → 3-4%.
- Competition + US concentration compress FCF-adj margin to ~18-19%.
- Multiple compresses to ~12x 2027E EPS (cyclicality discount deepens);
  2027E EPS ~$18 (below consensus). DCF floor + multiple compression.
- Trigger: 2 consecutive quarters of negative B2B growth OR Adj-EBITDA
  margin contraction >100bps.

BASE (50%) — IV ~$380:
- Rev growth decelerates 9.4%→~4%; FCF-adj margin →21%; WACC 10.5%,
  g 2.5%. Moderate re-rating to ~16x 2027E EPS. (The DCF base above.)

BULL (25%) — IV ~$490:
- B2B + AI + OneKey sustain ~8% growth; FCF-adj margin →23-24%;
  platform premium (Engine-3 overlay) re-rates multiple to ~21x 2027E
  EPS (partial peer convergence). DCF bull corner (WACC 9.5%, g 3.0%)
  ≈ $464 + platform premium ≈ $490.
- Trigger: B2B >25% growth for 4 qtrs + FCF-adj margin >22% + OneKey
  engagement inflection.

Expected IV = 0.25×270 + 0.50×380 + 0.25×490 = $380
50% CI: $323–$464 (DCF corners). 80% CI: $270–$490 (scenario range).
MoS = (380 − 321.63)/380 = 15.4% → "Limited-to-Adequate" (right at the
15% boundary). NOT a strong margin of safety — consistent with the stock
being near 52-wk highs.

SECTION 4.5. TIME-HORIZON ARBITRAGE
────────────────────────────
Market-implied horizon: At 7.5x TTM EV/FCF and 13.7x 2027E P/E, the
market is pricing roughly 1-2 years of current earnings with a LOW
terminal multiple — i.e., it is treating EXPE as a near-term/cyclical
asset, NOT a long-duration compounder. My horizon: 3-5 years (the DCF
explicit window) + terminal. Spread ≈ 2-3 years. This IS a potential
arbitrage IF the market reclassifies EXPE from "cyclical" to
"compounder" — but that reclassification requires SUSTAINED proof
(B2B + margin expansion for 4-8 more quarters). It is not guaranteed;
hence the scale-in (not lump-sum) recommendation.

SECTION 5. CONVICTION & POSITION SIZING
────────────────────────────
Conviction (0-3 each, /15):
1. Business quality: 3 (46% ROIC, asset-light, FCF machine, wide-on-
   paper moat)
2. Valuation attractiveness: 1 (MoS only ~15%; stock within 4% of 52-wk
   high; FCF yield 11.5% is good but the multiple has already re-rated)
3. Macro alignment: 2 (weak-dollar tailwind, offset by sticky inflation)
4. Thesis clarity (KPIs): 2 (clear KPIs, but post-2026 path is
   assumption-heavy)
5. Execution traceability: 3 (20 qtrs B2B double-digit, consistent
   margin expansion, raised guidance, disciplined buybacks)
TOTAL = 11/15 → HIGH (10-12).
Conviction decay: -1 in 6 months unless B2B growth + margin expansion
re-confirm (next 2 prints are the test).

Sizing: High conviction → 6-8% cap, BUT reduced for (a) thin MoS,
(b) proximity to 52-wk high, (c) terminal-value uncertainty → 4-5%
initial. Scale to 6-7% ONLY on a pullback to $290-300 (which restores
MoS to ~25-30%). No Engine-4/5 cap applies (Engine 1). Macro is a mild
tailwind, not a headwind, so no forced split — but I still scale in
given entry price.

SECTION 5.5. BEHAVIORAL & POSITIONING
────────────────────────────
- Short interest: 8.42% of float, 7.84M sh, days-to-cover 5.44,
  MoM change -16.4% [Pack/Aggregator]. Moderate-high; a squeeze is
  possible on a beat but NOT a primary thesis driver.
- Institutional ownership: 106.49% [Pack] — >100% implies heavy
  lending/ETF overlap; vulnerable to passive-flow reversals.
- Insider: 0.61% [Pack] — low (dual-class; Diller's Class B is the real
  control, ~32% voting [Actual]). No cluster-buying signal.
- Sentiment: Stock +25% since Apr-2026, near 52-wk high → momentum is
  FROthy; consensus is already "Buy" (mean PT $333.86, only +3.8%
  upside [Pack]). The easy money has been made. This argues AGAINST
  chasing and FOR scaling in.
- Crowding risk: 8/15 (moderate-high — consensus Buy, near highs, high
  institutional). → position size -1%p (already reflected in 4-5%).

SECTION 6. PORTFOLIO FIT
────────────────────────────
EXPE adds: consumer-discretionary/travel exposure, a high-FCF/low-net-
debt cash generator, and a weak-dollar beneficiary. It is a good
DIVERSIFIER to a tech-heavy book (different demand driver: travel vs.
capex/AI) but CORRELATES with (a) US consumer health and (b) the
dollar. If the portfolio is already long US-discretionary + short the
dollar, EXPE adds little new risk. Best fit: a core "quality compounder
at a discount" slot in a balanced book.

SECTION 6.5. KELLY SIZING
────────────────────────────
From $321.63: Bull $490 (+52%), Base $380 (+18%), Bear $270 (-16%).
Treat "win" = base-or-better (75%), "loss" = bear (25%).
Avg win = (57.4+18.4)/2 ≈ +$38 (using $/sh: bull +168, base +58 → avg
+113); loss = -52.
b = 113/52 = 2.17; p=0.75, q=0.25.
Full Kelly f* = (0.75×2.17 − 0.25)/2.17 = (1.63−0.25)/2.17 = 0.636.
0.25x Kelly = 15.9%. The high Kelly reflects the asymmetric payoff
(+18% base vs -16% bear) but OVERSTATES confidence because the IV has
a wide CI and the terminal value dominates. I CAP at the conviction-
based 4-5%. Gap (15.9% vs 5%) = 10.9%p < 20%p → no forced re-analysis,
but the gap confirms I am deliberately UNDER the Kelly (appropriate
given terminal-value uncertainty and entry price).

SECTION 7. RISKS & CATALYSTS
────────────────────────────
RISKS:
1. Travel cyclicality / US recession (the #1 bear trigger) — pro-
   cyclical, US ~60% of revenue.
2. Competitive erosion: Airbnb (vacation rental/Vrbo), Booking
   (scale), Google (metasearch) — the "narrow moat" durability question.
3. US concentration + FX: non-US is the faster segment but adds
   translation + geopolitical risk (Middle East disruptions noted in
   [brief/Estimate]).
4. Capitalized-software capex (unconfirmed) could be higher than filed
   PP&E-only capex → FCF overstated.
5. Governance: dual-class (Diller 32% voting), short-seller/activist
   attention [brief/Estimate].
6. Sticky inflation (3.4%) suppressing discretionary travel.
CATALYSTS:
1. B2B growth sustaining >20% (20+ qtrs already).
2. Adj-EBITDA margin expansion (+1.5-1.75pts guided FY26) → FCF margin
   re-rating.
3. OneKey loyalty inflection (data/lock-in).
4. AI-driven cost efficiency.
5. $5B buyback authorization (share-count shrink → EPS leverage).
6. FIFA World Cup summer-2026 demand [brief/Estimate].
7. Multiple re-rating if reclassified "cyclical → compounder."

SECTION 7.5. CORRELATION-ADJUSTED RISK
────────────────────────────
Common bear trigger with other US-discretionary/long-duration holdings:
a US recession + rising real rates would hit EXPE AND most growth
names simultaneously (tail correlation → 1 in stress). EXPE's weak-
dollar benefit is a PARTIAL hedge if the portfolio is long the dollar
or has international revenue. Conditional VaR (worst 5%): a recession
scenario (Bear, 25% weight) implies ~-16% to -30% drawdown; I size to
tolerate a -30% single-name drawdown at 4-5% weight (= -1.2 to -1.5%
portfolio impact). If the book is already >15% US-discretionary, reduce
EXPE weight to avoid stacking the recession trigger.

SECTION 8. MONITORING RULES (Thesis Integrity)
────────────────────────────
Re-evaluate / EXIT if ANY:
- B2B gross bookings growth turns NEGATIVE for 2 consecutive quarters.
- Adj-EBITDA margin CONTRACTS >100bps y/y for 2 consecutive quarters
  (mix/AI thesis broken).
- FCF-adj margin (my ~19-21% path) prints >150bps BELOW my path for 2
  quarters (capex/SBC surprise, e.g., capitalized software).
- Regime shifts to Recession (>50% prob) with EXPE rev growth <3%.
- Governance/activist event that changes control or strategy materially.
- Short interest >15% of float with a published substantive short report
  (adversarial data trigger).
ADD on: pullback to $290-300 (MoS → 25-30%) with B2B + margin intact.
KPI dashboard (quarterly): B2B growth %, Adj-EBITDA margin, FCF-adj
margin, take rate (rev/gross bookings), OneKey engagement, buyback $,
net debt.

SECTION 9. RED TEAM (Adversarial / Short Thesis)
────────────────────────────
1. "Narrow moat, not wide": Airbnb owns vacation rental (Vrbo's home
   turf), Booking has global scale + lower US concentration, Google
   owns the metasearch entry point. EXPE's US-centric B2C is a
   shrinking share of a competitive market. (My 13/21 moat score is
   generous; the market's "narrow" label may be right.)
2. Cyclicality is under-appreciated: travel is the FIRST discretionary
   spend to cut in a recession; 7.5x EV/FCF may be FAIR, not cheap,
   for a pro-cyclical asset. The DCF's 2.5% terminal growth may be too
   high for a mature, competitive marketplace.
3. FCF is overstated: filed capex excludes capitalized software (a real
   outflow for a tech marketplace); TTM OCF margin (33%) is a timing
   artifact, not a run-rate. True sustainable FCF margin may be ~17-18%,
   not 21%.
```
